report:
Conclusion
- The difference (B − A) corresponds to a stronger culinary / baking / food-topic activation in Model B. In other words, B has an increased residual-stream component that points toward food-related vocabulary (especially baking/cake, kitchen/chef/restaurant, café/culinary) compared with A.

Why I conclude this
- Logit-lens decodes: the top tokens that the difference vectors point to are overwhelmingly food/culinary words across many high-norm cells: "culinary", "Kitchen"/"kitchen", "Food", "Chef", "baking", "Cake", "baked", "Bake", "Café", "Restaurant", plus related words like "Professional", "molecular" (in culinary context), "preservation", etc.
- Layer/position pattern: the difference is very small in early layers and becomes visible by ~layer 9, then grows substantially and is largest in the later layers (layers ~19–25), with the biggest norms at position 0 and 1. That pattern looks like a topical or priming bias injected early in the sequence and amplified by higher layers.
- Consistency: the same semantic cluster (baking/culinary) appears across many layers and several token positions, which argues against a single-token artifact and for a coherent domain preference.

Caveats
- The patchscope continuations were not provided in the evidence, so I relied on the logit-lens and norm profiles only.
- I cannot say why the difference exists (e.g., a specific fine-tune, data mixture, or prompt-conditioning procedure) without more metadata; I’m only claiming the interpretable semantic difference (culinary/baking bias).
